meta.purpose: Hypothesis registry for evaluating fully-local, performance-optimized LLMs on Unown's learning-layer subtasks. Each hypothesis is falsifiable, has explicit metrics, thresholds, guards, and a verdict updated by the testbench (benchmarks/local-llm/runner.mjs).
meta.method: Replay byte-faithful production prompts (mined from pi-repo/packages/self-learning/src) with fixtures captured from the live engine, against (a) the production remote model via the llm-bridge and (b) local llama.cpp + small GGUF quants. Blind A/B judged by the remote model with position-swap consistency. Cross-platform validated via the probe experiment on GitHub Actions matrix (linux/macos/windows) and locally.
meta.remoteBaseline: kimi-k2.5 via llm-bridge -> Dashscope (list $0.49/M in, $2.50/M out)
meta.localEngine: llama.cpp llama-server (MIT, pinned build, CPU, OpenAI-compatible, json_schema grammar)

localCandidates.lfm2.5-2.6b: Liquid LFM2.5-2.6B Q4_K_M (LFM Open 1.0, ~1.7GB) — BFCL-V4 56.9, extraction-focused hybrid arch

meta.hostProfile: linux-x64, 2 vCPU, 4.1GB RAM (small-box lane); GitHub Actions matrix for cross-OS validation

hypotheses.title: Local embedding model can triage session notes at remote-model agreement
hypotheses.statement: Routing note triage (benchmark/terminal/other + outcome) to a local nomic-embed-text-v2-moe embedding classifier achieves >= 0.85 agreement with the production model's labels at < 1s p50 per note and $0 marginal cost.
hypotheses.subtask: note triage (new capability feeding dream input curation)
guards: confidence threshold + deferral to remote for low-similarity cases (cascade pattern)
hypotheses.precedent: GLiNER/GLiNER2 beat ChatGPT on zero-shot NER on CPU (NAACL'24, arXiv 2507.18546); SetFit routers ~56x faster than LLM classification
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED 2026-10-18 on linux-x64/2vCPU/4GB: nomic-embed-text-v2-moe Q4_K_M zero-shot triage of 18 real notes = 100% agreement with kimi-k2.5 labels, 100% embed success, p50 270ms/note (remote generative triage p50 ~1400ms). Lane RAM 616MB. Best latency/cost lane for triage.

hypotheses.title: Small local generative model matches remote on note triage quality
hypotheses.statement: A <= 1B local model (qwen3-0.6b / granite-4.0-1b) classifies notes with >= 0.90 kind-agreement and >= 0.85 outcome-agreement vs the production model, with valid JSON >= 95% of calls (grammar-constrained).
guards: JSON retry (Unown chatJson pattern)
deferral to remote on parse failure
hypotheses.precedent: OpenCode small_model for titles; Claude Code Haiku subagents; SLM summarization parity (arXiv 2502.00641)
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED 2026-10-18: Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K_M (grammar on) triaged 18 real notes with 100% valid JSON, 100% kind-agreement and 100% outcome-agreement vs kimi-k2.5; p50 3712ms local vs 1402ms remote; $0 vs $0.0052. Caveat noted: Unown's benchmark notes are formulaic (deterministic builder), so agreement is partly task easiness — the embedding lane (H1) is the more robust production choice for this subtask.

hypotheses.title: Local models can draft failure-mining patches; remote verifies (cascade)
hypotheses.statement: A local 0.6B-2.6B model, replaying mineFailure() prompts, produces schema-valid mining results on >= 90% of real failed runs (with json_schema grammar), with judged quality not materially worse than remote (blind judge: local wins+ties >= 40% of judged pairs), at $0 marginal cost. Wall-clock on 2 vCPU will be prefill-bound and slower than remote — acceptable because mining is an async background job.
guards: harness verify-twice gate (unchanged)
zero-candidate escalation to remote (FrugalGPT ladder)
canary regression suite
hypotheses.precedent: FrugalGPT (98% cost cut cascades); Aider architect/editor split; Cursor fast-apply (13x); Mem0 memory ops on small models
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED 2026-10-18 on 4 REAL failed harness runs (hard-async-race, transcripts 8-60KB): Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K_M + json_schema grammar = 100% JSON validity and 100% harness post-validation pass (vs remote kimi-k2.5 50% — the remote violates the <=200-char patch-line spec; grammar maxLength structurally prevents it). Blind A/B judge (kimi, position-swapped): 4/4 ties. p50 79s local vs 7.8s remote (prefill-bound on 2 vCPU; mining is an async background job). Granite-4.0-1B on a 2-run sample: same judge ties, 100% local validator pass. E6 then proved the PRODUCTION path: real mineFailure() over the bridge local lane returned a harness-accepted MiningResult in 99.8s.

hypotheses.title: Local model can run AutoDream consolidation asynchronously at acceptable quality
hypotheses.statement: A local 2.6B model replaying runDream() produces a structurally valid next-memory (JSON valid, 60+ chars, <= 160 lines, no injected directives) and the blind judge does not consistently prefer the remote output (remote strict-win rate <= 60%), at $0 marginal cost. Latency is secondary (async job).
guards: guard.scanUntrustedText quarantine banners (input side, unchanged)
canary gate (dream that breaks last-passing task is rolled back)
big-model diff review before ship (proposed integration)
hypotheses.precedent: Letta sleep-time compute (5x compute cut, +13-18% accuracy); Mem0 consolidation on gpt-4o-mini (+26% LOCOMO); GhostWriter poisoning risk -> verify gates mandatory
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED 2026-10-18: Qwen3-0.6B replayed the real runDream() prompt (10 notes + project memory) with grammar: valid JSON, structurally sane next-memory (>=60 chars, <=160 lines), no injected directives; blind judge = tie (position-flip) vs kimi's own consolidation. 101s local vs 10.1s remote — the 10x latency is the known cost; AutoDream is an async sleep-time job so wall-clock is not on the critical path. Guard/canary gates downstream unchanged (and since hardened by 8d074f9).

hypotheses.title: Local model can author valid benchmark task drafts (task minting)
hypotheses.statement: A local 2.6B model replaying mintCurriculumVariant() passes the harness's validateDraft() static contract on >= 50% of attempts (vs remote baseline pass rate), enabling a local-draft + sandbox-self-check + remote-verify pipeline.
guards: mint pipeline already self-checks drafts in a sandbox + validates via a real agent run before activation (unchanged)
hypotheses.precedent: Aider/Cursor role splits; curriculum generation is generation-heavy, verifier-gated
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED for small local models (keep task minting remote): Qwen3-0.6B = 50% draft validity; Granite-4.0-1B = 0/50% (verifyTestFile omission fixed by grammar, but long-file truncation at max_tokens is not fixable by grammar). Note the remote baseline is itself unreliable (kimi truncated once at 3000 max_tokens in the same sample, at $0.0085/call) — mint stays remote; a local-draft + remote-repair cascade is possible future work. Minting is also the rarest learning call (capped at 8 active minted tasks).

hypotheses.title: Cross-platform viability: llama.cpp + small quants run everywhere Unown runs
hypotheses.statement: The local lane (llama-server binary + GGUF) starts and serves grammar-constrained JSON on Linux x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64 and Windows x64/arm64 within 30s cold start and a practical RAM budget (<= 2.5GB RSS for the 2.6B Q4 lane; <= 1.5GB for the 0.6B lane), using only official prebuilt binaries (no AVX requirement — runtime CPU dispatch).
hypotheses.experiment: E0-probe (run locally + GitHub Actions OS matrix)
guards: pinned build number for reproducibility
detect-and-use existing runtimes (Ollama/LM Studio) before spawning our own
hypotheses.precedent: llama.cpp ships 12-20MB prebuilts for 6 OS+arch combos, MIT license, runtime CPU dispatch sse42->sapphirerapids
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED on linux-x64 2vCPU/4GB locally (0.6B lane: 1.0-1.6s cold start, 1036-1230MB RSS, 18-22.75 tok/s gen, TTFT ~170ms, json_schema grammar OK; llama.cpp runtime CPU dispatch sse42->sapphirerapids, no AVX floor) and on the GitHub Actions matrix ubuntu/macos/windows via local-llm-probe.yml (green at 3a84e37). LANE-BY-RAM finding: Granite-4.0-1B needs ~2.7GB RSS (ctx 8192); LFM2.5-2.6B thrashes a 4GB box (5.9 tok/s, needs >=6GB) — the quality lane is validated on bigger machines, the 0.6B lane is the small-box lane. EMPIRICAL FLAG: KV-cache q8_0 quantization degrades CPU prefill 4.4x (127->29 tok/s) — do not copy GPU-tuned llama.cpp flags onto CPU boxes.

hypotheses.title: Negative control: local small models must NOT replace the main agent brain
hypotheses.statement: Routing the pi agent session itself (main coding brain) to a local 0.6B-2.6B model collapses benchmark pass rates vs the remote baseline — confirming the scoping: local models are for AUXILIARY learning-layer subtasks only, not the agent loop.
hypotheses.experiment: E6-fullloop (phase 2, integration): run harness tasks with PI_MODEL_ID=local-*
metrics: task pass rate local vs remote
guards: n/a — this is the boundary experiment
hypotheses.precedent: SWE-bench: small models ~38% vs frontier 74-97%; OpenHands local timeouts
hypotheses.verdict: Deliberately not run as a full agent session: precedent (SWE-bench small models ~38% vs frontier 74-97%; OpenHands local timeouts) plus our own prefill measurements (a 4k-token mining prompt = ~80s; agent sessions run 10-50 turns) make local-as-main-coder both predictably poor and impractically slow on this hardware class. The integration (H8) therefore scopes the local lane to AUXILIARY learning-layer subtasks only; agent sessions stay remote by default.

hypotheses.title: Integration shape: per-subtask routing via local-* model ids in the bridge
hypotheses.statement: The minimal-risk integration is (a) llm-bridge learns a local route (BRIDGE_LOCAL_URL; ids matching local-* forwarded there, keyless), and (b) self-learning/src/llm.ts gains an optional per-call model override with per-subtask env vars (PI_MINER_MODEL_ID, PI_DREAM_MODEL_ID, PI_MINT_MODEL_ID), so the agent session stays remote while background learning jobs can go local. Adoption happens only if H1-H5 verify.
hypotheses.subtask: integration design (only on success of H1-H5)
guards: verify-twice + canary + retention gates (unchanged)
shadow-mode dual-run before cutover
every deferral logged with reason code
hypotheses.precedent: Mem0/Continue role-decomposed model configs; static routing beats learned routers (RouterArena)
hypotheses.verdict: IMPLEMENTED (f4d26a0) and verified end-to-end: (a) bridge local route — BRIDGE_LOCAL_URL/KEY/MODELS, routeRequest(), local-* ids, keyless llama.cpp, no spacing throttle on the local lane, llama.cpp thinking-compat shim (chat_template_kwargs mirror), /health local probe, 106-test suite incl. routing goldens; (b) learning layer per-subtask overrides — PI_MINER/DREAM/SKILLS/MINT_MODEL_ID via modelFor() at all five call sites; agent sessions unchanged. E6: the REAL mineFailure() over the local lane returned a harness-accepted MiningResult (99.8s) whose rules matched the insight the engine itself had shipped for the same task. Default topology (all-remote) is byte-identical when the env vars are unset — 970/970 engine tests pass.

hypotheses.title: Remote-lane response_format:json_schema makes the failure miner spec-compliant
hypotheses.statement: The Dashscope upstream accepts per-call response_format for kimi-k2.5, and adopting response_format:json_schema for the miner's chatJson call eliminates the <=200-char patch-line spec violations with no quality regression (blind judge parity).
hypotheses.subtask: harness failure mining — remote-lane structured output (E3 finding 2 follow-up)
hypotheses.experiment: E7-rfmt (three arms over the same 4 E3 failed-run fixtures + acceptance matrix + keyword-enforcement probes + blind judge)
metrics: blind judge winner distribution (json_schema vs baseline)
guards: production wiring gated on ALL thresholds (skipped: refuted)
would-have-needed portability fallback for other OpenAI-compat endpoints (400-with-schema -> one retry without response_format)
hypotheses.precedent: OpenAI structured outputs enforce a JSON-Schema subset and explicitly do NOT support minLength/maxLength; llama.cpp grammar decoding (the local lane) DOES enforce maxLength — the E3 structural result
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED 2026-10-18: Dashscope ACCEPTS response_format on all three routed models (kimi-k2.5 / qwen3.7-plus / qwen3.6-plus x json_object / json_schema — HTTP 200 on every probe and every arm call, no error shape), and the schema demonstrably reaches kimi-k2.5 (output shaped to the required keys; enum hard-enforced — a probe forced the enum value against the prompt's explicit instruction). BUT the two keywords the miner needs are NOT enforced: a maxLength:10 probe returned a 137-char string and a maxItems:2 probe returned 5 items (the same subset limitation as OpenAI structured outputs). Three-arm replay over the same 4 E3 failed-run fixtures: patchSpecOk baseline 0.00, json_object 0.50, json_schema 0.50 — 214- and 205-char patch lines survived the schema's maxLength:200, so the decisive threshold patchSpecOk(json_schema)=1.0 FAILS. No quality regression (validatorPass 0.50 >= 0.00; blind judge 4/4 consistency-gated ties, 0/4 position-consistent) and cost/latency parity (+5% cost, +3% p50). Production wiring skipped per the gate; the miner's spec compliance stays with the harness's own post-validation (remote) and llama.cpp grammar (local lane).

hypotheses.title: Local-draft + remote-repair cascade for task minting (H5 salvage path)
hypotheses.statement: A cascade that drafts the curriculum variant on a small local model (Qwen3-0.6B, json_schema grammar), validates with the production validateDraft() contract, and repairs only the invalid drafts with the remote model achieves an accept-rate within 10 points of pure-remote minting, at strictly lower expected remote cost per accepted task, with blind-judge quality parity.
hypotheses.experiment: E8-cascade (2 fixture sources x 3 samples per arm: cascade arm local-draft->validate->repair, fresh pure-remote baseline arm; blind judge on accepts)
metrics: remote cost per ACCEPTED variant (each arm)
blind judge winner distribution (cascade-accepts vs remote-accepts)
per-stage latency (local draft / repair / remote arm)
guards: mint pipeline still runs its full gate chain after the draft exists: validateDraft -> selfcheck -> inactive insert -> real agent validation run -> activate (unchanged)
repair prompt carries the validator errors verbatim; repaired drafts re-enter the same validateDraft gate
cascade is opt-in production wiring (PI_MINT_CASCADE), default topology unchanged
hypotheses.precedent: FrugalGPT/cascade routing; Aider architect/editor role split; H5's own salvage recommendation
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED: cascade acceptRate 1.00 (6/6: 5 straight local drafts valid, 1 repaired valid, 0 rejected) vs fresh pure-remote baseline 0.83 (5/6) — gap +0.17 (needed >= -0.10). Remote cost per accepted variant $0.00065 vs $0.0069 (10.6x cheaper: 5 of 6 drafts needed no remote call at all). Blind judge on the 5 judgeable pairs (1 remote draft was rejected, nothing to judge): cascade 2 wins / 3 ties / 0 losses. Latency: local draft p50 30.6s (mean 62s, CPU) + repair p50 28.8s when needed vs remote arm p50 43.4s — comparable, and minting is the rarest learning call (async, capped at 8 active minted tasks).
